summary: Full-chapter abridgment of 'Berlin (1858-1859)' that keeps all eight verbatim excerpts and each essential beat in source order: the fourth-child rationale and the Civil Law absurdity; the Persia gale and tourist mathematics; Chester, Eaton Hall and Dickens's England; the Black District with Marx hindsight; eighteenth-century London and its later shrinking; Antwerp; the one-lecture university; Sumner and Apthorp; the Gymnasium indictment with the dynamo image; the accidental Beethoven awakening; and the closing resolution against Berlin.
acceptable_changes: Cut the captious-critic argument; 'Strictly followed, the rule would have obliged them' becomes 'the family' so the pronoun still has a referent.

Cut G. P. R. James, the Mersey gale, Charles the First, Little Nell, the Adelphi coffee-room and most of the Piccadilly catalogue, per the optional list. Two London images remain: Fleet Street/Johnson and the Piccadilly chariots.

Cut Antwerp's Baron Osy, dancing peasants, Ostade/Teniers and Alva. The cathedral and wine image remain, and the 'kneeling at the foot of the Cross' sentence is kept whole. The 'Even in art... Descent from the Cross' sentence stays to set up the later reference.
Compressed the Berlin arrival and the professor passage. The student judgments now keep only accent and beer.
Cut 'William Tell', the Kaiser-at-the-window detail, the diet and Thiergarten tramps, and German society and theatre remarks. Bismarck is reduced to one clause on inertia.
Reduced Kant/Hegel/Goethe/Schiller to one clause. Kept the Wagner coda together with 'Near forty years passed.'
risks: Section balance is approximate. The opening and travel sections may run somewhat over their budgets, and the Gymnasium section somewhat under. Overall length is aimed at 2200 but cannot be verified in this call.
Removing 'what he expected' and 'a week's experience' from the Berlin arrival slightly speeds the transition from Antwerp.
review_focus: Sumner's quotation and Apthorp's school suggestion sit in separate paragraphs, each with clear attribution.
The Marx clause and the 'fifty years afterwards' London passage read as narrator hindsight, not the boy's knowledge.
Heine appears in the student scene before 'smacked of Heine' and the 'derisive Jew laughter of Heine'.
The beer-hall setting precedes the Beethoven awakening, which is framed as 'accidental, unintended, unforeseen.'
The transition from 'London... felt and hated' to 'Education went backward' to Antwerp.
